footer.coverage: Two sources, kept apart on purpose. Vacancy counts are live openings registered at the Czech Labour Office (Úřad práce ČR) — real postings, though the register leans toward service, trades and operational roles, so higher-skill and senior corporate counts read low. Every salary figure comes instead from the official ISPV earnings survey and its regional RSCP cut: what people are actually paid, not what a posting advertises. Figures are workplace-based, so a region reflects what employers there pay rather than what residents earn. Where the survey has no figure, we leave it out rather than estimate it.

With uniform weights the cross-scheme re-scoring is a no-op (the order cannot change), so this run does not establish the ranking is weighting-independent, only that no weighting difference exists to test.

email.notWiredHowTo: Anything that can POST reaches it today — an automation (Zapier/Make), a form, or a mail-parsing service. To turn on real forwarding, route an inbound-email provider (Postmark, SendGrid or Mailgun inbound) at this endpoint and set EMAIL_INBOUND_DOMAIN to the domain it accepts mail on. email.gmail4: Create a Filter (e.g. Subject contains “application”) → Forward it to . Every matching email now flows in automatically.

about.title: What the platform does
about.intro: From the original CV-analysis acceptance criteria to the v2 matching platform and its HR automation. Pick a capability to read how it works, drawn as a live component diagram: <moss>moss</moss> is automated, <coral>coral</coral> is a deliberate human gate, and <dashed>dashed</dashed> arrows are optional or asynchronous steps.

students.exampleIntro: Three illustrative students against one junior backend role. Each carries a bounded, evidence-driven weighting — the axes are the same, how much each counts is earned. The real version of this table lives in Decisions → Group evaluation.
students.caseBadgeTitle: Fed by the case-grounded phases — these ratings gate observed minting
students.scoringFootnote: Hover a rating for the verbatim evidence behind it — no quote, no score. Adéla's case-tagged constructs average 4.3 on quoted evidence — above the 4/5 minting bar, so her case-grounded interview itself minted the observed skills that narrow her band. Bára outscores her on potential but stays wide until something is observed; Cyril's fluent delivery is scored separately from the content of his reasoning (and his 2s on the case constructs mean nothing is minted).
students.scriptIntro: The thought-script the agent follows (~{min} minutes), shown in its case-designed form. The skeleton is fixed — concrete → mechanism → counterfactual → metacognitive — and the agent may improvise follow-ups, but the highlighted phases draw their questions from the role's designed case, so every candidate works the same material. Hints are injected on purpose: coachability only exists live.
students.scriptFootnote: Every rating must cite a verbatim transcript quote (no quote, no score), a short or evasive answer widens the confidence band instead of lowering the score, and reasoning content is scored separately from delivery fluency — nerves and non-native English are not weak thinking. When the case-fed constructs all rate on quoted evidence and average above bar, the interview itself mints observed-provenance skills onto the candidate's profile.

emptyLedger.title: Nothing sealed yet
emptyLedger.lede: A case does not just ask a candidate to write code. It records how the work was made, and seals that record so you can trust what you are reading.
emptyLedger.controlsHeading: What a sealed submission will carry

hashChain.name: Tamper-evident hash chain
hashChain.proves: Every observed step is chained server-side as it happens, so a session cannot be quietly rewritten afterwards. A link that fails to recompute — or a client clock that contradicts when the server received the event — marks the whole trace untrustworthy rather than merely odd.

promptCapture.name: Prompt capture
promptCapture.proves: The assistant and stakeholder exchanges the candidate wrote are part of the record. Model use is graded on how they drove it — decomposition, iteration, asking it to verify itself — never on volume, and never as a penalty.

canaries.name: Planted canaries
canaries.proves: The starter repo carries deliberate flaws, each with one checkable truth. Every one comes back addressed, flagged, propagated or unverifiable — a planted flaw that survived into the submission is generated output that was shipped unread.

perturbation.name: Mid-flight perturbation
perturbation.proves: A requirement moves while the work is open, server-timestamped. Everything after that moment is adaptation to a brief no prepared answer anticipated; absorbing it is judgment you can watch happen.

watermark.name: Session watermark
watermark.proves: Each session's work carries its own reference. Another session's reference turning up inside this one is decisive evidence a solution circulated between candidates. A narrow control, deliberately: on its own, a missing marker is a note for the reviewer, never a verdict.

baseline.name: Frozen baseline comparison
baseline.proves: At approval the case is solved once by a bare model with nobody steering it, and that answer is frozen. Submissions are compared against it. Never a penalty — it tells you where to aim the authorship interview, not what to score.

emptyLedger.pasteTrace: Alongside them, one bulk paste with no incremental build-up reads as suspect — and a suspect submission is held for the live interview that verifies authorship, never auto-advanced on score.
emptyLedger.honestDarkness: Every verdict above is shown to you with its own evidence, including where a check could not run: a control that did not fire is never displayed as one that passed. None of it starts until a case exists — define the need and the engine designs the assignment these controls wrap around.

motivation.description: Genuine interest in the role and the team.

problem_decomposition.label: Problem decomposition
problem_decomposition.description: How they break down an unfamiliar problem: surfacing assumptions, constraints, and structure before reaching for a solution.

anchor.1: Restates the problem or jumps to a memorized answer; no decomposition.
anchor.2: Names a few parts but misses key constraints or dependencies.
anchor.3: Breaks the problem into coherent sub-problems and states the main constraints.
anchor.4: Decomposes cleanly, surfaces hidden assumptions, and asks clarifying questions before committing.
anchor.5: Reframes the problem to expose its core, prioritizes sub-problems by risk, and reasons about edge cases unprompted.

learning_agility.label: Learning agility
learning_agility.description: How they learn and recover when stuck: evidence of a repeatable loop, not a one-off success.

anchor.1: Cannot describe how they learn or how they got unstuck; credits luck or other people.
anchor.2: Describes passive learning (watched tutorials) with no reflection on what worked.
anchor.3: Names a concrete learning strategy and one thing they would do differently.
anchor.4: Shows a deliberate diagnose-experiment-adjust loop with a real stuck-then-recovered example.
anchor.5: Transfers a lesson from one domain to a new one and reflects on how their approach itself is improving.

coachability.label: Coachability
coachability.description: How they take a hint, correction, or pushback in real time: integrate it, deflect it, or freeze.

anchor.1: Ignores or reflexively defends against the hint.
anchor.2: Acknowledges the hint but cannot act on it.
anchor.3: Adjusts after the hint, with some prompting.
anchor.4: Integrates the hint quickly and explains how it changes their approach.
anchor.5: Probes the hint, asks a sharpening question, and generalizes it beyond the immediate problem.

conceptual_depth.label: Conceptual depth
conceptual_depth.description: Whether they understand why, not just what: tested with counterfactuals and transfer to novel cases.

anchor.1: Recalls definitions but cannot explain why; breaks down on any 'what if' variation.
anchor.2: Explains the happy path but not tradeoffs or what changes under different conditions.
anchor.3: Explains the mechanism and handles a simple counterfactual.
anchor.4: Reasons about tradeoffs and adapts the concept to a changed requirement.
anchor.5: Derives the idea from first principles and predicts where it breaks under a novel constraint.

motivation_direction.label: Motivation & direction
motivation_direction.description: Coherence and specificity of why this field and this role: intrinsic drive over rehearsed answers.

anchor.1: Generic or purely extrinsic ('good pay'); no specific interest.
anchor.2: States interest but cannot tie it to anything they have actually done.
anchor.3: Gives a specific, consistent reason grounded in a real experience or project.
anchor.4: Shows a coherent throughline from past choices to this role and a forward goal.
anchor.5: Articulates a sharp, self-aware direction with evidence of self-driven exploration toward it.

communication_collaboration.label: Communication & collaboration
communication_collaboration.description: Clarity and structure of explanation, active listening, and how they work with other people's input.

anchor.1: Disorganized or evasive; does not address the question asked.
anchor.2: Answers but rambles or lacks structure; hard to follow.
anchor.3: Clear, structured answers; listens and responds to the actual question.
anchor.4: Explains complex ideas simply and checks for understanding.
anchor.5: Adapts the explanation to the listener and surfaces disagreement constructively.

clinical_judgment_patient_safety.description: Sound clinical reasoning, scope-of-practice awareness, and a patient-safety-first instinct under pressure.

scientific_rigor.description: Experimental rigor, data integrity, and honest reasoning about evidence, limitations, and reproducibility.

craft_portfolio_depth.description: Depth and originality of craft evidenced by real work — the portfolio, not just stated skills.

operational_execution.description: Reliable execution at scale: throughput, prioritization, and steady judgment when volume or exceptions spike.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: How KandiDate processes candidate and workspace data: consent, retention, erasure, AI transparency, subprocessors and billing.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: KandiDate is hiring software. It reads CVs, runs interviews and records hiring decisions, so this policy is written around the data those features actually touch. It describes shipped behavior, and where a control is configurable, it says so.

roles.title: Who is responsible for your data
roles.controller: For candidate data (CVs, interview transcripts, scorecards and decision records), the company running the hiring workspace is the data controller. It decides why and how candidates are assessed.
roles.processor: The KandiDate vendor acts as a processor for that data: it processes candidate data only to provide the product to the controller, under the controller's configuration and instructions.
roles.account: For the customer's own workspace account and billing data, the KandiDate vendor is the controller.

data.title: What the product processes
data.intro: The product processes only what the hiring flow needs:
items: CV documents and the text extracted from them
Voice interview audio, transcripts and structured scorecards
Job-fit scores, evidence and salary estimates derived from the CV
Decision records: who was advanced, rejected or offered, when, and why
Contact details used to reach a candidate about their application
Workspace account, plan and usage data for the customer

consent.title: Consent and retention
consent.gate: Consent is captured before any AI reads a candidate's data, and candidate pages state that an AI is involved before it happens, not after.
consent.retention: Recruitment consent expires. In this deployment the retention window is up to {months} months from the moment consent is given. The window is configurable per deployment, and the figure shown here is derived from the live configuration rather than typed by hand, so it cannot drift from what is enforced.
consent.expiry: When consent expires, the record is anonymized: the name is reduced to a non-identifying handle, contact details, the CV text and verbatim quotes are removed, and non-identifying recruitment signals (skills, scores, seniority, salary band) are retained so the controller can keep lawful hiring statistics.
consent.readGate: Expiry also takes effect immediately at read time: the product withholds CV text and transcripts even before the periodic anonymization sweep has run, and suppresses any further outreach to that candidate.

rights.title: Your rights as a candidate
rights.intro: Every candidate receives a personal token link. It requires no account, and it opens a page where you can:
items: See the data held about you, including the decisions recorded about your application
Ask for human review of any decision an AI was involved in
rights.erasure: Erasure runs as a single transaction across your profile, interview transcripts, scorecards and the message outbox: it completes in full or not at all.
rights.carveout: One category is exempt from erasure: sealed decision records. They are retained under Article 17(3)(b) and (e) GDPR, because a regulated hiring decision must remain auditable and defensible after the fact. Once you are erased, they refer to you only by a masked, non-identifying reference.

voice.title: Voice interviews
voice.body: A voice interview is recorded and transcribed only after you explicitly consent on the interview page. That consent is enforced on the server: without it the interview session is never created and no transcript is stored. You can decline, and your application continues without a voice interview.

ai.title: AI transparency
ai.oversight: Under the EU AI Act, screening, scoring, ranking and interviewing candidates is a high-risk use. Every candidate-facing page shows an AI disclosure before an AI reads your data, as Article 50 requires.
ai.sealed: No candidate is advanced, rejected or offered by the machine alone. Every adverse decision requires a human, and every decision, human or automated, is sealed into a tamper-evident audit record stating who made it and why.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.body: The product routes to the providers each customer configures, so the set it can engage is: {list}. None of them is mandatory: a self-hosted, offline installation engages no external processor at all. Candidate data is never sold or shared, and is never used to train models.
subprocessors.trustLink: The maintained list, together with the product's article-by-article EU AI Act posture, is published on the trust page.

billing.title: Billing data
billing.body: Paid plans are sold through Polar, acting as merchant of record. Polar processes payment details and issues invoices; card data never reaches KandiDate. The product stores only the subscription state needed to meter usage.

security.title: Security
items: Provider API keys are stored write-only and encrypted at rest; they never round-trip to a browser
Each workspace's data is isolated per tenant
Decision records are sealed into a tamper-evident hash chain with key rotation
An offline mode blocks all model egress, for air-gapped and in-VPC installs

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For requests about your data as a candidate, use the token link from any message the product sent you; it is the fastest, verified path. For anything else, contact the operator of this deployment or write to {email}.

meta.description: The terms for using KandiDate: the service, plans and billing through Polar, customer responsibilities for candidate data, and the AI system disclosure.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of KandiDate, a hiring workspace that analyzes CVs, runs AI voice interviews, verifies work samples and records hiring decisions. By creating a workspace or using the product you agree to them.

service.title: The service
service.body: KandiDate provides software for assessing job candidates: job-fit scoring, AI voice interviews, verified work samples, scheduling, candidate communication and a sealed record of hiring decisions. The product assists assessment; it does not make hiring decisions on its own, and it is designed so that it cannot.

accounts.title: Workspaces and accounts
accounts.body: You are responsible for what happens in your workspace: keeping access credentials confidential, the lawfulness and accuracy of the data you provide, and the conduct of the people you invite.

billing.title: Plans and billing
billing.polar: Paid plans and metered interview minutes are sold through Polar, which acts as merchant of record: Polar handles checkout, payment processing, invoicing and applicable taxes. Subscriptions renew until cancelled and can be managed or cancelled through the customer portal.
billing.meters: Plan limits are metered in human terms (candidates, work-sample cases, interview minutes), never in tokens. When an allowance runs out, the related feature pauses until the allowance renews or is topped up; your data is unaffected.

customerData.title: Candidate data and your responsibilities
customerData.controller: For candidate data processed in your workspace, you are the data controller and the KandiDate vendor is your processor. You are responsible for having a lawful basis, informing candidates, honoring their rights, and configuring the retention window that matches your jurisdiction.
customerData.processor: Candidate data is processed only to provide the service to you. It is never sold, never shared beyond the subprocessors you configure, and never used to train models.

ai.title: AI system disclosure
ai.highRisk: KandiDate screens, scores, ranks and interviews candidates. Under the EU AI Act this is a high-risk use, and the product is built accordingly: human oversight on every adverse decision, sealed and attributable decision records, and candidate-facing AI disclosures.
ai.deployer: If you run KandiDate on your candidates, you take on the deployer obligations of Article 26, including assigning human oversight and informing candidates. The product operationalizes those duties but does not remove them. No statement in the product or on these pages is a claim of certified conformance.

use.title: Acceptable use
items: Do not use the product to make fully automated hiring decisions; the human-review controls must not be circumvented
Do not upload candidate data you have no lawful basis to process
Do not use the product to discriminate on protected characteristics
Do not probe, overload or attempt to breach the service or other tenants' data

ip.title: Your data, our software
ip.body: You keep all rights to the data you and your candidates bring. The vendor keeps all rights to the software. On termination you can export your workspace, and you can request erasure of hosted data.

warranty.title: Warranties and disclaimers
warranty.body: The service is provided as is. Scores, salary estimates, transcripts and other model outputs are decision support, not guarantees, and their accuracy cannot be warranted. Nothing in the product or on these pages is legal advice.

liability.title: Liability
liability.body: To the extent permitted by law, the vendor's aggregate liability for claims arising from the service is limited to the amounts paid for it in the twelve months before the claim. Hiring decisions remain the customer's own: by law and by the product's design, they are made by people.

termination.title: Termination
termination.body: You can stop using the service and cancel a paid plan at any time through the customer portal. The vendor can suspend a workspace that violates these terms, with notice where practicable. Sealed decision records survive erasure as described in the privacy policy.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by the law of the Czech Republic, where the product is built and primarily offered. Mandatory consumer and data-protection rights in your jurisdiction remain unaffected.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: These terms may change as the product evolves. Material changes are announced in the product before they take effect; the date above states the current version.

control.title: Autonomy control room
control.intro: Human oversight for the autonomous hiring pipeline — a kill switch, the human gates awaiting you, and an immutable audit trail of every automated decision (the record-keeping a high-risk AI hiring system requires).

autonomy.pausedBody: Auto-advancement is halted; lifecycles wait for you. Resume to continue + reconcile.

outcomes.heading: Outcomes & calibration
outcomes.blurb: Record what actually happened to promoted candidates; the engine calibrates the promote floor against reality — does a higher predicted score really convert? You apply the suggestion, so the learning loop stays human-in-the-loop.

rationale.insufficient: Not enough resolved outcomes yet to calibrate (need ≥ {min}).
rationale.weak: Scores are only weakly predictive — hire rate doesn't rise cleanly with the score. Investigate the rubric before moving the floor.
rationale.raise: Candidates below {suggested} rarely converted; the floor of {current} is letting weak matches through. Consider raising it to {suggested}.
rationale.lower: Candidates from {suggested}–{current} converted well; the floor of {current} may be too strict. Consider lowering it to {suggested}.
rationale.calibrated: The floor of {current} is well-calibrated — it sits at the first band where most promoted candidates were hired.
